q7.answer: The raw token is generated in memory at request time and put into the email job payload on the queue, which the worker uses to build the link. Only sha256(token) is inserted into password_resets, so the raw token exists only in the job and the email.

q8.answer: The server computes sha256 of the token from the URL and looks up the password_resets row by token_hash (UNIQUE). It is good only if a row exists, used_at is NULL and expires_at is in the future; otherwise the 'this link has expired' page is shown. The same check runs on page load and again on submit.

q9.answer: It is not a separate counter. It is computed by counting password_resets rows for the user with created_at within the last hour, including killed and used rows. Old requests drop out as their created_at passes the 1-hour window, and an optional cleanup job only deletes rows more than 1 hour past expiry.

q10.answer: In the same transaction that inserts the new row, and after the rate-limit check passes, all of the account's rows with used_at IS NULL are marked used_at=now(). This kills the earlier links, so at most one link is live.

q11.answer: In one transaction: claim the link (conditional UPDATE setting used_at), update the user's password_hash, and delete all of the user's sessions rows. The 'password was changed' email is enqueued after COMMIT, outside the transaction.

q12.answer: The link claim is a conditional UPDATE (WHERE id=? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now()) inside the transaction. Only one submit updates a row; the other updates 0 rows, rolls back and sees the expired page.
